The numbers that can make or break a candidate The North-West’s 25.08 million registered voters make it Nigeria’s largest geopolitical voting bloc. The South-West follows with 19.61 million, ahead of the North-Central, which has 16.97 million. The political significance is unmistakable. Kano, Kaduna and Katsina are among the country’s most populous electoral states, while Lagos leads the national register with 7,488,633 voters. A candidate who makes substantial gains across these states can dramatically improve his national tally. Yet neither zone is a political inheritance. The North-West contains competing party structures, influential local leaders and voters whose choices are shaped by security, economic conditions, personalities and the performance of elected officials. Kano’s political history, in particular, shows how a powerful state-level movement can disrupt calculations made in Abuja. The South-West presents a different challenge. Tinubu’s longstanding political network gives him an advantage, but it does not guarantee uniform support across the region. Lagos demonstrated this in 2023 when Obi defeated Tinubu there by 9,848 votes, polling 582,454 against the president’s 572,606. That result remains a reminder that even a candidate’s home territory can become a battleground. Party loyalty, local grievances, urban voting patterns and the credibility of candidates can all upset expectations. The numbers also require caution. INEC’s register measures people registered to vote, not the number who will eventually cast ballots. Turnout, voter accreditation, election-day logistics and the distribution of votes among candidates will determine how much of that numerical advantage translates into electoral power. What elections since 1999 reveal Nigeria’s presidential elections have repeatedly shown that regional strength matters most when it forms part of a wider national coalition. Olusegun Obasanjo’s victories in 1999 and 2003 rested on support extending beyond his South-West origins. Umaru Musa Yar’Adua’s 2007 victory reflected the strength of the Peoples Democratic Party’s national machinery, while Goodluck Jonathan’s 2011 success drew on substantial support in the South and parts of the North. The 2015 election changed the political landscape. Muhammadu Buhari’s victory demonstrated that an opposition alliance could defeat an incumbent when it combined a formidable northern base with support in other parts of the country. The merger that produced the All Progressives Congress brought together political interests that had previously competed against one another. Buhari’s re-election in 2019 again showed the importance of maintaining a broad electoral coalition, even as the contest exposed persistent regional divisions. Tinubu’s 2023 victory followed another complex pattern. He won the presidency with 8,794,726 votes, ahead of Atiku’s 6,984,520 and Obi’s 6,101,533. The result was not the product of one region alone. It reflected a combination of Tinubu’s South-West support, votes from the North and the fragmentation of opposition support across several candidates. The lesson for 2027 is not that a candidate must reproduce one previous election formula. It is that regional dominance, without alliances and sufficient support elsewhere, can leave a candidate short of victory. The 2023 result that changed the game The last election exposed the risks of treating Nigeria’s regions as predictable voting blocs. Tinubu secured 2,542,979 votes in the South-West and 2,652,235 in the North-West, according to zonal breakdown. The figures showed that his northern performance was at least as important as his home-region strength. But the North-West did not vote as a single political unit. Atiku won Kaduna with 554,360 votes against Tinubu’s 399,293, while Rabiu Kwankwaso carried Kano for the New Nigeria Peoples Party. The split deprived the opposition of a unified northern vote while also limiting Tinubu’s ability to sweep the region. In the South-West, Obi’s narrow victory in Lagos demonstrated that Tinubu’s political base could be challenged. Obi’s strength in the South-East, meanwhile, did not translate into enough votes across the country to secure the presidency. Atiku’s support in parts of the North also proved insufficient. The distribution of votes made the difference. Had opposition support been concentrated behind a single candidate, the contest could have looked very different. Instead, three major contenders divided the electorate, while Tinubu assembled enough votes across several regions to finish first. Simon Kolawole, veteran journalist and political analyst, captured the strategic calculation in his assessment of the 2023 presidential election result. “Tinubu did well in ‘two out of three’ – the South-West and the core North,” he surmised. Kolawole also noted that a winning candidate might need sizeable support from the North-Central or South-South, or both, in addition to strength in the South-West and core North. His point is central to the next contest: Commanding two major blocs may create a strong platform, but it does not remove the need to win elsewhere. The constitutional hurdle also remains. Under Section 134 of the Constitution, a presidential candidate must secure the highest number of votes cast and at least one-quarter of the votes in no fewer than two-thirds of the states and the Federal Capital Territory. Regional strength must therefore translate into both a national plurality and geographically distributed support. Fasoranti died on Tuesday at the age of 100 years. Before his death, the Yoruba group had been engulfed in leadership crisis. It is instructive to note that Afenifere hinges on a traditional, non-competitive succession process to choose its next leader. However, the body faces the critical task of unifying its historically fractured factions. While the old guards like Chief Olu Falae express hope that a new leader will emerge seamlessly through ancestral custom, key insiders paint a much bleaker picture of the group’s future. How division set in In 2023, its then Acting Leader, late Pa Ayo Adebanjo, rocked the boat by suspending two of its officials, the National Publicity Secretary, Jare Ajayi and National Organising Committee, Abagun Kole Omololu. The suspension, however, led to a split and worsened the crisis. Adebanjo had said: “I will tell you the story and I won’t go further. Pa Fasoranti phoned me on Friday that Tinubu had phoned him and that he wanted to come and see him and he wanted to say no. I said no, don’t do that, you are an elder statesman. Falae, who is now a monarch, rules out the possible division within the Yoruba fold. He said Afenifere was a self-perpetuating and self-regulating organisation in which leadership emerged through an established process rather than through competition for positions. “Leadership chooses itself. A new leader will emerge without any struggle. “It is obvious who the next leader will be, and I hope and pray it will be so this time,” he said. Is reconciliation a tall order? A senior Afenifere leader had confided in Vanguard that the reconciliation was to be unveiled immediately after the 2027 general elections. item.title: Ebola in Nigeria: Fears contacts could test positive mount
item.description: •Prof Tomori asks authorities to prepare •Nigeria’s real test is inside its hospitals •Can health workers count on running water, sanitizer, protective equipment? By Chioma Obinna The tap is there. But is there water? The sanitiser dispenser is mounted on the wall. But is it filled? And if a patient walks into a hospital with symptoms that raise suspicion of a dangerous infection, will the health worker attending to that patient have the protective equipment needed to stay safe? These questions may sound routine. By Chioma Obinna The tap is there. But is there water? The sanitiser dispenser is mounted on the wall. But is it filled? And if a patient walks into a hospital with symptoms that raise suspicion of a dangerous infection, will the health worker attending to that patient have the protective equipment needed to stay safe? These questions may sound routine. But as Nigeria confronts a confirmed case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease, they go to the heart of a more difficult question: how prepared are the country’s hospitals to prevent another outbreak? Nigeria has been here before. The 2014 Ebola outbreak tested the country’s ability to detect an imported infection, trace contacts and prevent wider transmission. The COVID-19 pandemic later exposed the importance of hand hygiene, personal protective equipment and infection prevention and control in health facilities. Emergency measures were introduced. Isolation facilities were established, surveillance was strengthened and health workers were trained to respond to infectious threats. But what happens when the emergency passes? Do the taps still run? Are protective supplies replenished? Can hospitals still isolate suspected cases safely? And do health workers have the equipment and practical support to implement the precautions they have been trained to observe? For infectious disease experts, Nigeria’s latest Ebola alert is a reminder that preparedness cannot be measured by emergency announcements alone. It must be evident in the wards, consultation rooms and emergency units where patients first seek care. One confirmed case, a nationwide test Nigeria’s latest Ebola alert followed the confirmation of an imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the patient, a woman with a recent travel history involving Uganda, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital in Abuja on October 11. Laboratory tests confirmed the infection on October 20. Authorities identified 44 contacts for monitoring, including people who might have been exposed during the patient’s healthcare visits and travel. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) activated its incident management system, while surveillance and infection-prevention measures were strengthened. By October 23, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, said the patient was showing signs of recovery. There was no evidence of community transmission in the information released at that point, although investigations and contact monitoring were continuing. Genomic analysis also found that the virus detected in Nigeria was genetically related to the strain identified in Kenya’s index case. Pate cautioned that this similarity did not, by itself, establish a direct epidemiological link between the two patients or explain precisely how the infection reached Nigeria. The response is therefore unfolding on two fronts. Authorities must establish whether anyone else has been infected, while ensuring that hospitals can recognise and safely manage any suspected cases that emerge. Second responsibility That second responsibility is particularly important. A patient with fever, headache, vomiting or diarrhoea may have any of several illnesses. But when the symptoms are accompanied by a relevant exposure history, health workers must know what questions to ask, whom to notify and how to protect themselves and others while the patient is assessed. An outbreak may be detected by a laboratory, but preventing further transmission also depends on what happens at the patient’s first point of contact with the health system. When the basics cannot be taken for granted Running water, soap, hand sanitisers, cleaning materials, protective equipment and safe waste disposal rarely command the attention given to emergency operations centres or laboratory testing. Yet these ordinary provisions underpin the safe delivery of healthcare. A tap without water cannot support handwashing. An empty sanitiser dispenser offers little protection. Personal protective equipment that is missing when needed can leave a health worker unable to follow the precautions required when caring for a suspected infectious case. The problem is not necessarily that every Nigerian hospital lacks these facilities. It is that their availability, functionality and reliability cannot be assumed. A UNICEF Nigeria WASH Gender Landscape Analysis published in January 2025 reported that only six per cent of healthcare facilities assessed had basic water, sanitation and hygiene services. The figure relates to the facilities covered by the assessment, rather than every hospital in the country, but it highlights a significant infrastructure challenge. For Ebola preparedness, the implications are immediate. Infection prevention is not simply a matter of displaying instructions on a hospital wall. It requires dependable water supplies, adequate consumables, appropriate protective equipment, trained staff and systems that ensure these resources are available where and when they are needed. The association has also advocated the reactivation of infection prevention and control committees and emergency drills to test the readiness of healthcare workers. Its warning is straightforward, doctors and other health workers should not attend to suspected Ebola patients without appropriate protective equipment or manage them in open wards where other patients and staff could be exposed. These are not special provisions to be considered only when Ebola appears. They are basic requirements for a health system expected to manage infectious diseases safely. item.title: Blaming opposition for hunger is delusional — Atiku
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Olayinka Ajayi Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused President Bola Tinubu of shifting responsibility for Nigeria’s economic hardship to the opposition, insisting that the administration must account for its record ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Read Also: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), was reacting to Tinubu’s remark at the APC campaign flag-off in Kaduna on Saturday that the opposition created hunger and poverty in the country. In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku described the President’s comment as “either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia”. “The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record,” he said. Atiku accused Tinubu’s administration of worsening the hardship faced by Nigerians, arguing that the President could not dismiss concerns about the cost of living by blaming political opponents. He also criticised Tinubu’s planned inauguration of a section of the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway, alleging that the ceremony showed how disconnected the President was from the daily realities of Nigerians. “A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon cutting ceremony,” he said. The former Vice President challenged the administration to explain the removal of the petrol subsidy and the depreciation of the naira, which he claimed had fallen from about ₦471 to ₦1,329 to the dollar. He also cited a World Bank estimate that 63 per cent of Nigerians would be below the national poverty line in 2026, accusing the government of presiding over rising poverty. Atiku further questioned the extension of the 2024 budget into 2025 alongside a separate 2025 budget, as well as what he described as ₦7.13 trillion recorded under “energy security” in 2024 and ₦11.2 trillion in NNPC pipeline-related spending. item.title: Alvarez apologises to Atletico fans after summer exit attempt
item.description: Julian Alvarez apologised to Atletico Madrid fans on Saturday for trying to leave the club during the summer, admitting he understands why supporters were angry with him. The Argentina international was heavily linked with Barcelona this summer and said during the World Cup he thought it would be best if Atletico sold him. The Rojiblancos refused to accept an offer from the Catalan giants and Alvarez was whistled and jeered by the club’s own fans at the start of the season. However, the tension has gradually eased and Alvarez netted his first goals of the season this week, firstly against Stuttgart in the Champions League and then on Saturday helping the club beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0. “I wanted to apologise to our people for my words during the World Cup,” Alvarez told Movistar. “The truth is it was a mistake on my part, both in how I expressed myself and the timing. Above all because I understand people’s anger — I would have been angry too, as a fan. “And also because of how they’ve stuck by me and supported me all these years and in these last few weeks. They’ve been very generous, and I really value that.” Atletico signed the 26-year-old from Manchester City in 2024 and he has become a key figure for Diego Simeone’s side over the previous two seasons. Alvarez put in his brightest display of the season against Deportivo and his goal split the teams at the Metropolitano stadium. “I’m starting to feel good… I’m grateful to all my teammates because they’ve supported me,” continued Alvarez. “They’ve really stuck by me throughout this whole time… and I’m working to improve. “I’ve felt better in these last few matches… both physically and with the ball.” AFP The post Alvarez apologises to Atletico fans after summer exit attempt appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: New York Archdiocese agrees to pay $800m to sex abuse victims
item.description: The Archdiocese of New York said Saturday it had agreed to a settlement in which the church would pay more than $800 million to hundreds of victims of sexual abuse by clergy. The agreement, to be formally signed in early November, marks the end of years of negotiations with lawyers representing the plaintiffs, as the American Catholic Church has been mired in sexual abuse scandals since the early 2000s. “We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks wrote in an email sent to his priests and forwarded to AFP by the archdiocese. According to The New York Times, which broke the story, each of the approximately 1,300 victims will receive at least $250,000, and potentially more depending on the severity of the abuse suffered. item.title: Alvarez fires Atletico to win against Deportivo
item.description: Julian Alvarez continued on his road to redemption by scoring the only goal as Atletico Madrid beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0 on Saturday to close the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona to two points. Diego Simeone’s side are second, with champions Barca hosting Real Madrid, third, in the Clasico at Camp Nou on Sunday. Alvarez netted for the second consecutive game, having grabbed his first of the season in Atletico’s 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart in midweek. Atletico supporters hounded Alvarez during his first appearances this season after he tried to force his way out of the club in the summer, but the tension has gradually cooled. Home fans at the Metropolitano stadium directed a few whistles at the team in general after a slow start, with Deportivo having the best chance of the first half. Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved well from Lorenzo Amatucci, while at the other end Diego Simeone’s side lacked spark. Early in the second half Alvarez found the breakthrough. Alejandro Grimaldo fired in a dangerous low pass towards the far post, where the Argentina international turned it over the line. Alvarez came close to a second after a slick team move, with Alex Baena slipping him in, but Depor goalkeeper Leo Roman saved the striker’s attempted lob with his face. The former Manchester City striker looked much closer to his best form in this outing after struggling with some fitness problems earlier in the campaign. Alexander Sorloth lashed narrowly over from a tight angle as Atletico sought to kill off the game, unsuccessfully. Deportivo might have levelled in stoppage time with Kevin Sanchez volleying well wide from Adama Traore’s cross when well placed to trouble Oblak. The Galicians’ best chance came with virtually the last kick of the game, with Oblak saving from Sanchez on his line, when the forward seemed destined to score. Earlier, Georges Mikautadze snatched a late 2-1 win for Villarreal in a derby clash against Valencia, who had midfielder Harvey Elliott sent off as both sides finished with 10 men. The Yellow Submarine came from behind to triumph, climbing into mid-table and leaving Javier Aguirre’s Los Che 19th, in the relegation zone. Pepelu sent Valencia ahead from the penalty spot in the first half before American defender Alex Freeman headed the visitors level at Mestalla stadium after 69 minutes. Inigo Perez’s Villarreal had Pape Gueye sent off when the Senegal international hit Jose Gaya in the face with his elbow. However, English midfielder Elliott, on loan from Liverpool, was soon dismissed for two quick yellow cards for apparent dissent. Villarreal striker Mikautadze broke through in stoppage time, racing through and finishing with aplomb to claim the three points. item.title: Obama blasts Trump’s ‘chaos and cruelty’ while campaigning for Democrats
item.description: Former US president Barack Obama delivered a scathing critique of his successor, Donald Trump, at a rally Saturday in Ohio to support Democratic candidates ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. “After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘Enough is enough,'” Obama declared in Cleveland. “We are voting for change right here in Ohio.” The 65-year-old Democrat blamed the Trump administration for the rising cost of living, a top voter concern amid soaring fuel prices. “The current president chose to make a series of bad decisions,” Obama said. “Most importantly, he decided to start an unnecessary war that nobody asked for.” Obama also urged voters to cast their ballots as soon as possible since early voting is already open in this northern industrial state. “Don’t procrastinate, don’t equivocate,” Obama said. The former president retains considerable popularity among the Democratic base, which he is keen to leverage to support his party’s candidates in the upcoming crucial elections that will decide control of Congress. In Ohio, former Democratic senator Sherrod Brown will attempt a comeback against incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted, while the race for governor will be contested between Democrat Amy Acton and Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a former presidential candidate in 2024. Polls for Ohio give Democrats a slight lead in both those races, but the results are expected to be close. Nationally, polls also suggest that Democrats could regain control of the House of Representatives but face a much more competitive contest for the Senate. After Cleveland, Obama will head north to Michigan this evening for a rally in Detroit alongside Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate candidate. While both of Michigan’s Senate seats are currently held by Democrats, El-Sayed, from the party’s left wing, is in a close race with Republican Mike Rogers. item.title: Trump votes early in Florida for US midterm elections
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Saturday voted early in his home state of Florida for the November 3 midterm elections, in which his Republican Party is battling to maintain control of Congress. Trump and his wife, Melania, cast their ballots ahead of an appearance by the president at a campaign rally in the southern US state of Georgia. Trump said he voted party line, or exclusively for members of his Republican Party. Asked by reporters after voting about corruption as a major issue for voters, Trump insisted that it was happening in districts and cities controlled by Democrats. “You ought to look at the real corruption — it’s Democrat corruption,” he said. The Republican billionaire, who has consistently refused to accept his defeat in the 2020 presidential election, baselessly alleging widespread voter fraud, reiterated allegations along those lines Saturday. “I ran and I won in 2016, and I won in 2020, too, but it didn’t work out that way,” he said at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office in West Palm Beach. “It was a rigged election, but I won by millions of votes.” With 10 days to go until the midterms, which traditionally favor the party outside the White House, Trump faces dismal polls suggesting the Republicans will lose control of the House of Representatives and possibly the Senate. Without a Republican majority in Congress, the 80-year-old president would have little room to push through his legislative agenda during his final two years in office. He or his staff could also face numerous congressional investigations by Democrats, who have said they want to examine business dealings conducted by the president and those close to him through the family’s holding company since his return to the White House. item.title: Southampton end West Ham’s unbeaten run, Burnley sack manager
item.description: Southampton ended West Ham’s nine-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 win at the London Stadium to surge into the Championship top six despite starting the season with a four-point deduction. Kyle Walker-Peters and Tomas Soucek replied for the Hammers, but there were swathes of empty seats and boos by full-time as they missed the chance to go top. “This is a tough place to come, against a quality team, and we knew we needed to start strongly, so we worked on that all week,” said Saints boss Tonda Eckert after his side went 2-0 up inside the opening 10 minutes. “They made it tough for us in the second half, so it was important that we stayed brave to bring the result over the line.” Burnley sacked manager Nicky Hayen after just 14 games in charge following his side’s 4-1 defeat at Lincoln, which left the Clarets in the relegation zone. item.description: The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Abdulaziz Yari, has pledged overwhelming support for President Bola Tinubu in northern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 election. I come again to thank you for that, to seek your mandate for the second term, to keep a promise on prosperity, continuity and progress. I have an argument, I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. Who created it? They did! They created hunger, they created poverty, we are trying to eradicate it,” he said. “We pay salaries regularly, our governors are working, I am proud of them, they are developing.
